## Docs Structure & House Style Report

### 1. **`docs/tools/` Directory Layout**

The directory contains ~40 markdown files covering development tools, terminals, editors, and infrastructure. Siblings for the LSP page include:
- **Editor & agents** section (line 135–144 in mkdocs.yml): OpenCode, specify-cli, SpecStory, Claude Code keybindings, codexbar, LLM
- **Shell & terminal**: ghostty, warp, starship, fzf
- Other: tmux, sesh, agent-overlays, containers, networking, etc.

**Alphabetical ordering**: The nav uses title-case display names with lowercase file paths. Within subsections, entries follow loose alphabetical order (e.g., "Agent overlays" < "Agent pane discovery" < "Agent skills").

### 2. **mkdocs.yml `nav:` Block**

The `Tools` section (lines 114–169) uses hierarchical grouping:
- **Editor & agents** (lines 135–144) — where LSP naturally belongs
- **Shell & terminal** (lines 122–130)
- **Sessions & worktrees** (lines 131–134)
- **Git & DevOps** (lines 146–156)
- **Productivity** (lines 157–163)
- **chezmoi conventions** (lines 165–169)

**Entry format**: `- Display Name: file/path.md` or just `- file/path.md` if the filename is self-explanatory.

Recommendation: Insert LSP under "Editor & agents" as:
```yaml
- Language servers (LSP): tools/lsp.md
```
(Alphabetically after "LLM" or before "OpenCode" depending on convention preference.)

### 3. **House Style for Tool Docs**

**From `ghostty.md` (comprehensive ~90-line example)**:
- **Opening**: One-sentence intro with link to official project.
- **Managed config**: Explicit filepath (`~/.config/ghostty/config`) + source path (`dot_config/ghostty/config`).
- **Key settings**: Bulleted explanations of what's managed and why (e.g., `macos-option-as-alt`).
- **Subsections**: Use `##` for logical topics (e.g., "xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote hosts").
- **Pitfalls/gotchas**: Prominent callout blocks (`> **Note**: ...`) for caveats.
- **Cross-links**: At end ("See also: [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config...").
- **Code blocks**: Triple backticks with language hint (`` ```ini ``, `` ```bash ``).
- **Length norm**: 1–3 KB per page; subsections are bite-sized.

**From `direnv.md` (compact ~50-line example)**:
- **One-liner concept**: "loads per-project environment variables".
- **File paths table**: Points to helper file, zsh init, prompt config.
- **Copy-paste config**: Provides a recommended `.envrc` snippet.
- **Behavior notes**: Explains equivalence (what it *doesn't* do vs `source activate`).
- **References**: External links to upstream docs.

**Conventions**:
- Headings: `# Title`, `## Section`, `### Subsection` (never start with `###`).
- Relative paths in cross-links use `../../dot_config/...` or `../sesh.md`.
- Code snippets are indented or in fenced blocks; shell output shown in plain text.
- "What's NOT managed and why" sections appear implicitly in callout boxes or a dedicated "What is intentionally NOT managed" table (see `agent-overlays.md` lines 121–134 for the pattern).

### 4. **Image Embedding**

No screenshot images found in the sample pages I reviewed. The `docs/assets/` directory exists but contains only **CSS and JavaScript** (`copy-to-llm/` plugin files), not media.

**Conclusion**: This repo does not embed images in tool docs. If needed, the convention would likely be `docs/assets/img/` (following MkDocs Material convention), but none currently exist.

### 5. **Pitfalls / Backlog Cross-References Touching LSP, NeoVim, or Language Tooling**

**Pitfalls** (relevant to LSP/NeoVim):
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md` — Neovim 0.12 startup crash from avante/lualine calling `vim.fs.find` with stale cwd. Excellent reference for "what can break" in the plugin ecosystem.

**Backlog**:
- None explicitly mentioning LSP or language servers found in the search.

**Recommendation**: Your LSP page should cross-link to these pitfalls in an "Upstream plugins & pitfalls" section, especially the tree-sitter one (tree-sitter is a core LSP/syntax-tree dependency).

```text
1	# Ghostty & cmux
2	
3	[Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) is a fast, native terminal emulator. [cmux](https://cmux.dev/) is a lightweight macOS terminal built on Ghostty for managing AI coding agents. Both read the same config file.
4	
5	## Managed config
6	
7	This repo manages `~/.config/ghostty/config` (via `dot_config/ghostty/config`). cmux reads this file first (before `~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config`).
8	
9	Key settings:
10	
11	- **`macos-option-as-alt = left`** — Left Option sends Meta/Esc+ so tmux `M-` keybindings work (theme switching `M-c`/`M-t`, layouts `M-1`..`M-5`, fine resize `M-h/j/k/l`). Right Option retains macOS compose behavior for accents and special characters.
12	- **`font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig`** — Disables ligatures for code readability.
13	
14	> **Note**: Restart Ghostty/cmux after changing the config — it is read on launch, not hot-reloaded.
15	
16	Without `macos-option-as-alt`, macOS Option produces Unicode compose characters (e.g. `Option+c` → `ç`) instead of `Esc+c`, silently breaking all tmux Meta bindings. Alacritty and iTerm2 have their own equivalent settings (`window.option_as_alt` and Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+ respectively).
17	
18	## `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on remote hosts
19	
20	When you SSH into a fresh remote, `$TERM=xterm-ghostty` but the remote has no matching terminfo entry. Symptoms: broken line-drawing, garbled prompts, `clear`/`tput` failures, Neovim rendering glitches. This is especially visible on the first cmux/tmux SSH into a new box.
21	
22	### Option 1 — Ghostty built-in (recommended for interactive shells)
23	
24	> - [Shell Integration - Features](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration#ssh-integration)
25	
26	Add to `~/.config/ghostty/config`:
27	
28	```ini
29	shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo
30	```
31	
32	- `ssh-terminfo`: auto-installs `xterm-ghostty` on the remote the first time you `ssh` from an interactive shell with Ghostty shell integration loaded.
33	- `ssh-env`: forwards `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` via `SendEnv`, and falls back to `TERM=xterm-256color` where needed. The remote `sshd_config` needs a matching `AcceptEnv` line for the forwarded vars to take effect.
34	
35	**Limitations**: only triggers from interactive shells with the Ghostty wrapper active. It does not cover `ssh` invoked inside tmux/cmux panes, from scripts, or from wrapper tools (`rsync`, `aws`, `gcloud`, …). For those, use the manual helper below.
36	
37	### Option 2 — manual helper (works everywhere)
38	
39	A zsh function `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` is defined in [`dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh).
40	
41	```bash
42	ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
43	```
44	
45	What it does:
46	
47	- Validates local `infocmp` and the `xterm-ghostty` entry exist.
48	- Pipes `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` into a **single** SSH call (no double password/MFA prompt).
49	- On the remote: probes for `tic`, creates `~/.terminfo`, and runs `TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -` — so no root/sudo needed.
50	- Suppresses only the harmless `older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias` warning (emitted by ncurses < 6.3). Real errors still surface and set a non-zero exit.
51	
52	Example:
53	
54	```bash
55	# First time connecting a new box from cmux/tmux
56	ghostty-ssh-terminfo remote
57	# → Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote (in ~/.terminfo)
58	
59	# Verify
60	ssh remote 'infocmp xterm-ghostty >/dev/null && echo ok'
61	```
62	
63	### Smoke-test against `localhost`
64	
65	Yes — if `sshd` is running locally you can validate the function without touching a real remote:
66	
67	```bash
68	# Enable sshd (Linux)
69	sudo systemctl start ssh
70	# or macOS: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login
71	
72	ghostty-ssh-terminfo localhost
73	```
74	
75	Caveats:
76	
77	- `localhost` already has your own `$HOME`, so this effectively writes to the *same* `~/.terminfo` your local shell reads. Useful as a wiring/error-path smoke test, not as a representative "fresh remote" check.
78	- If you already have the entry locally (which you do, otherwise `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` would fail), the install is a no-op overwrite — still exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.
79	- For a cleaner test, point at a container or a VM where `xterm-ghostty` is definitely missing.
80	
81	## Why the warning appears (and can't be fully fixed client-side)
82	
83	The `|`-separated long description in Ghostty's terminfo is interpreted as an extra alias by `tic` / ncurses prior to 6.3. The entry still installs correctly; the warning is cosmetic. The only real fix is upgrading ncurses on the remote.
84	
85	## See also
86	
87	- [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config and keybindings (cmux runs on top of tmux).
88	- [sesh](../sesh.md) — session picker used in the tmux setup.
89
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/tools/direnv.md`

```text
1	# direnv
2	
3	`direnv` loads per-project environment variables as you enter and leave directories. In this repo it is initialized from Zsh, while prompt display is handled by Starship.
4	
5	- **Helper file**: `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` (chezmoi source: `dot_config/direnv/direnvrc`)
6	- **Zsh init**: `~/.config/zsh/tools/30_direnv.zsh`
7	- **Prompt**: `~/.config/starship.toml` via Starship's `[python]` module
8	
9	## Python `.venv` helper
10	
11	This repo provides `layout_python_venv [venv_dir=.venv]`.
12	
13	- Activates an existing virtual environment directory
14	- Does not auto-create `.venv`
15	- Delegates activation to `layout python3`
16	- Watches the venv marker files so creating `.venv` later triggers a reload on the next prompt
17	
18	## Recommended `.envrc`
19	
20	```sh
21	layout_python_venv
22	dotenv_if_exists
23	```
24	
25	Then allow it once per project:
26	
27	```bash
28	direnv allow
29	```
30	
31	You can target a non-default virtual environment directory if needed:
32	
33	```sh
34	layout_python_venv venv
35	dotenv_if_exists
36	```
37	
38	## Behavior Notes
39	
40	- Equivalent for daily use: `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PATH`, and `PYTHONHOME` handling come from direnv's built-in `layout python3`
41	- Not fully equivalent to `source .venv/bin/activate`: no `deactivate()` shell function and no direct `PS1` rewriting
42	- Prompt display still works because Starship reads `VIRTUAL_ENV` and shows the active environment name
43	- Leaving the directory automatically restores the previous environment
44	
45	## References
46	
47	- [Python · direnv Wiki](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/wiki/Python)
48	- [Activate python venv by default? · Issue #1264](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/issues/1264)
49	- [PS1 · direnv Wiki](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/wiki/PS1)
50
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Coding-agent CLI overlays (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex)
2	
3	This repo manages the *global* config files of three coding-agent CLIs via chezmoi `modify_` overlays:
4	
5	| CLI | Live file | Source script | Merge engine |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| Cursor | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | [`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl`](../../dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
8	| OpenCode (server/runtime) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
9	| OpenCode (TUI) | `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
10	| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) | Python `tomllib` + inline emitter |
11	
12	Overlay payloads live under [`.chezmoitemplates/agents/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/) and are sourced via `{{ template ... }}` includes so the merge logic can be tested independently of overlay contents.
13	
14	## Why `modify_` and not full file management
15	
16	All three CLIs **rewrite their config file at runtime** to record machine-local state: auth tokens, telemetry IDs, per-project trust grants, marketplace registrations with absolute paths, plugin-cache hashes, last-used provider hints, etc. Tracking the whole file as managed content would:
17	
18	1. Leak secrets (`authInfo`, `auth.json` content) into the dotfiles repo.
19	2. Bake one machine's absolute paths (`/Users/me/.codex/.tmp/...`) into another machine's apply.
20	3. Produce constant `chezmoi diff` noise as the CLI churns the file.
21	
22	The `modify_` overlay model deep-merges only the keys we explicitly enforce; everything else passes through verbatim.
23	
24	## What each overlay enforces
25	
26	### Cursor — [`agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json)
27	
28	```json
29	{
30	  "editor": { "vimMode": true }
31	}
32	```
33	
34	- `editor.vimMode = true` — universal preference; sibling `editor.fontSize` etc. survive the deep merge.
35	- **`permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays are intentionally NOT in the overlay.** `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at the same key path, so listing any entries here would clobber the user's live machine-specific allow-list on every `chezmoi apply`. Manage those per machine via the live file directly, or move to a `--argjson allow $merged` array-union approach if you ever need a shared baseline.
36	
37	### OpenCode — [`agents/opencode.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.overlay.json)
38	
39	```json
40	{
41	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
42	  "autoupdate": true,
43	  "default_agent": "build",
44	  "small_model": "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini",
45	  "agent": { "title": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } },
46	  "provider": {
47	    "github-copilot": {
48	      "options": { "timeout": 600000 }
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	- `$schema` — keeps editors aware of the schema for autocomplete.
55	- `autoupdate = true` — let the CLI self-update.
56	- `default_agent = "build"` — primary agent on TUI/CLI startup. Override per-session via `--agent` or the picker.
57	- `small_model = "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini"` — cheap model for title generation, summarisation, and other lightweight calls. Avoids billing Claude Opus quota for trivial tasks. Pairs with `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"`.
58	- `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"` — cheap completions for short title generation; sibling `agent.*` entries (per-agent provider, model overrides) survive.
59	- `provider.github-copilot.options.timeout = 600000` (10 min) — request-level timeout. Default is 5 min; bumped to give long Claude Opus generations more room before the SDK aborts the whole call. **Note**: `chunkTimeout` is intentionally NOT set here, see [docs/tools/opencode.md → Claude Opus stream stall](opencode.md#claude-opus-stream-stall-on-github-copilot) for the rationale (upstream bug [anomalyco/opencode#20466](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20466) — SSE-chunk-timeout errors aren't retried, so setting `chunkTimeout` would convert silent hangs into hard failures with no recovery).
60	
61	### OpenCode TUI — [`agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json)
62	
63	```json
64	{
65	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
66	  "keybinds": { "leader": "ctrl+x" },
67	  "mouse": true,
68	  "diff_style": "auto",
69	  "scroll_acceleration": { "enabled": true }
70	}
71	```
72	
73	The TUI lives in a **separate file** from server/runtime config: `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` with its own schema `https://opencode.ai/tui.json`. See upstream docs:
74	
75	- [Config → TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#tui) — file location, schema URL, precedence
76	- [TUI → Configure → Options](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/#options) — per-key semantics
77	
78	Key-by-key rationale:
79	
80	- `$schema = "https://opencode.ai/tui.json"` — TUI schema (different from `opencode.json`'s `config.json` schema). Lets editors validate + autocomplete.
81	- `keybinds.leader = "ctrl+x"` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Declaring it ensures muscle memory + the `<leader>` references in [docs/keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/) survive any future upstream default change. The other ~80 keybind defaults are intentionally NOT pinned here — they stay tracking upstream so new actions added by OpenCode become available without overlay churn.
82	- `mouse = true` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Trades terminal-native select-to-copy for OpenCode's in-TUI mouse support (scroll, click).
83	- `diff_style = "auto"` — adapts diff layout to terminal width (vs `"stacked"` which forces single-column). Pinning the upstream default makes intent explicit.
84	- `scroll_acceleration.enabled = true` — macOS-style smooth/accelerated scrolling. Per upstream docs this **takes precedence over and overrides** `scroll_speed`, so we deliberately omit `scroll_speed` from the overlay (setting both would mislead — the latter would be silently ignored).
85	
86	What's intentionally NOT in the TUI overlay:
87	
88	- `theme` — left unset so OpenCode's auto light/dark detection stays in effect (matches the system theme just like `ghostty` and the `tmux` theme switcher in this repo).
89	- Individual `keybinds.*` entries beyond `leader` — see above. fzf's shell-level `Ctrl+T` and OpenCode's `variant_cycle = ctrl+t` do not collide because they live in disjoint namespaces (shell prompt vs OpenCode TUI).
90	- `username_toggle` / `tips_toggle` / `display_thinking` — these are persisted by the TUI's `/help` customisation panel at runtime. Pinning them in the overlay would clobber the user's last in-app choice on every `chezmoi apply`, same anti-pattern as managing `plugin` paths or auth tokens.
91	- `scroll_speed` — see `scroll_acceleration.enabled` above; OpenCode ignores `scroll_speed` whenever acceleration is enabled.
92	
93	### Codex — [`agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml)
94	
95	```toml
96	personality = "pragmatic"
97	model = "gpt-5.4"
98	model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
99	
100	[features]
101	codex_hooks = true
102	unified_exec = true
103	shell_snapshot = true
104	steer = true
105	multi_agent = true
106	
107	[plugins."github@openai-curated"]
108	enabled = true
109	
110	[plugins."google-drive@openai-curated"]
111	enabled = true
112	
113	[plugins."computer-use@openai-bundled"]
114	enabled = true
115	```
116	
117	- Top-level model + reasoning preferences.
118	- `[features]` — opt into the experimental flags this user always wants on.
119	- `[plugins."<id>".enabled]` — curated plugin set; user-installed plugins appear under their own `[plugins."..."]` blocks and are preserved by the deep merge.
120	
121	## What is intentionally NOT managed
122	
123	| File / subtree | CLI | Why |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| `~/.cursor/{authInfo,auth*,privacyCache,statsigBootstrap,version,hasChangedDefaultModel,...}` | Cursor | Auth + telemetry; runtime-only. |
126	| `~/.cursor/{extensions,plugins,projects,worktrees,workers,browser-logs,chats,plans,prompt_history.json,argv.json,ide_state.json,agent-cli-state.json,ai-tracking,mcp.json,skills-cursor}` | Cursor | CLI-managed state, per-project, machine-local. |
127	| `~/.config/opencode/{node_modules,package.json,bun.lock,package-lock.json,plugins/}` | OpenCode | Node runtime + locally-installed plugin source trees. |
128	| `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` keys outside the TUI overlay (`theme`, `keybinds.*` other than `leader`, `username_toggle`, `tips_toggle`, `display_thinking`, `scroll_speed`) | OpenCode | TUI runtime customisation panel persists user choices here; overlay only pins stable preferences. |
129	| `~/.codex/auth.json` | Codex | OpenAI auth token. **Never** check in. |
130	| `~/.codex/[projects."<absolute-path>"]` | Codex | Per-project trust grants — absolute paths are machine-specific. **Round-tripped** by the modify_ script (see below). |
131	| `~/.codex/[marketplaces.<id>]` | Codex | Marketplace registrations with absolute `source = "/Users/.../.codex/.tmp/..."` paths. **Round-tripped**. |
132	| `~/.codex/{installation_id,history.jsonl,session_index.jsonl,sessions/,logs_*.sqlite*,state_*.sqlite,cache/,tmp/,log/,sqlite/,memories/,vendor_imports/,shell_snapshots/,models_cache.json,plugins/,skills/,rules/,ambient-suggestions/,version.json,AGENTS.md,.tmp/}` | Codex | Sessions, logs, sqlite, plugin/skills directories, machine-local notes. |
133	
134	The `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` presence-gates the entire `~/.cursor/`, `~/.codex/`, and `~/.config/opencode/` trees with a `stat` check so uninstalled CLIs never produce phantom directories.
135	
136	## How the Codex TOML merge works
137	
138	`jq` doesn't speak TOML and `mikefarah/yq`'s TOML emitter produces invalid output for keys with special characters (e.g. `github@openai-curated`). The Codex `modify_` script uses Python instead:
139	
140	1. Read live file into a `dict` via `tomllib` (Python 3.11+ built-in; `tomli` fallback for 3.10).
141	2. Pop `[projects]` and `[marketplaces]` subtrees into `state`.
142	3. Read overlay TOML into a `dict`.
143	4. Deep-merge: `live_minus_state <- overlay <- state`. Argument order is merge precedence (later wins). State wins last so per-project trust never gets clobbered by an overlay churn.
144	5. Emit TOML via a 30-line writer that quotes all non-bareword keys (handles `github@openai-curated` and `/Users/me/foo`-style project keys).
145	
146	The script falls through to passing the live file untouched if `python3` or `tomllib`/`tomli` are missing; chezmoi will skip the file for that apply.
147	
148	## OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration
149	
150	OpenCode docs now recommend `opencode.json` as the canonical filename, but installations from before that change use `config.json`. The repo manages only the modern filename; a one-shot script handles the migration:
151	
152	- [`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`](../../run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl) runs once per source-state hash, before chezmoi deploys files. It:
153	  1. No-ops if `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is absent.
154	  2. If only the legacy file exists: rename it to `opencode.json`.
155	  3. If both exist: deep-merge legacy into modern (modern wins on conflict, since it's presumed newer), then delete legacy.
156	
157	After this script runs, the `modify_opencode.json` overlay enforces the managed keys on the unified file. The legacy filename never reappears because OpenCode itself only writes `opencode.json` going forward.
158	
159	The migration script can be removed from the repo a few months after rollout (once all machines have run `chezmoi apply` at least once); it is idempotent and a no-op on fresh machines, so it's safe to leave indefinitely.
160	
161	## Refresh recipe
162	
163	To change what an overlay enforces, edit the corresponding `.chezmoitemplates/agents/<cli>.overlay.{json,toml}` file. Do **not** `chezmoi add` the live config — that would strip the `modify_` prefix and overwrite the script with the runtime file (which contains your secrets).
164	
165	To pull a new key from the live file into the overlay (e.g. you changed a Cursor permission you want shared):
166	
167	```bash
168	# 1. Inspect the live file
169	jq . ~/.cursor/cli-config.json
170	
171	# 2. Edit the overlay JSON / TOML and add the key
172	$EDITOR .chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json
173	
174	# 3. Verify the rendered modify_ script outputs what you expect
175	chezmoi execute-template < dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl > /tmp/m.sh
176	chmod +x /tmp/m.sh
177	cat ~/.cursor/cli-config.json | /tmp/m.sh
178	
179	# 4. Apply
180	chezmoi apply
181	```
182	
183	## Tests
184	
185	[`tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`](../../tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats) covers:
186	
187	- Each overlay enforces its declared keys.
188	- Live runtime keys outside the overlay are preserved verbatim.
189	- Codex `[projects.*]` and `[marketplaces.*]` round-trip unchanged (the round-trip property is the load-bearing invariant — break it and machines start clobbering each other's per-project trust).
190	- The modify_ scripts are idempotent (running output through the script again produces the same output).
191	- The OpenCode migration handles all three input states: legacy-only, both-present, neither-present.
192	- The Claude hook-aware merger (see next section): notify.sh added when missing; CodeIsland entries preserved; idempotency on re-apply; non-hook deep-merge preserves user siblings.
193	
194	Run with `just bats` (or directly: `bats tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`).
195	
196	## CodeIsland integration (macOS-only)
197	
198	[CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) is a macOS notch-area HUD (positioning analogous to [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar)) that surfaces real-time activity from 11+ coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Trae, Qoder, Factory, CodeBuddy, Kimi). It works by injecting per-CLI hook entries that fire `~/.codeisland/codeisland-bridge` (or `codeisland-hook.sh`), which streams events over a Unix socket at `/tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock` to the SwiftUI app.
199	
200	### Why macOS-only
201	
202	- Swift app, requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.
203	- The notch UI assumes a MacBook display geometry.
204	- Distribution is via brew cask (`wxtsky/tap`) or `.dmg`.
205	
206	There is no Linux fallback — the wire format depends on the macOS-specific bridge binary and socket path. We deliberately install nothing for CodeIsland on Linux and skip all related concerns there.
207	
208	### Install
209	
210	The `codeisland` cask is added in [`dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](../../dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) inside the `{{ if .installAiDesktopApps }}` block alongside the other agent desktop apps:
211	
212	```ruby
213	tap "wxtsky/tap"
214	cask "codeisland"
215	```
216	
217	### How we coexist with the app
218	
219	CodeIsland's settings panel calls itself "Auto hook install" with "auto-repair and version tracking" — meaning the **app actively writes and re-writes** hook entries into each detected CLI's config on every launch. Two coexistence patterns:
220	
221	> **Note (2026-04-25)**: CodeIsland v1.0.23 dropped `ExitPlanMode` from the default `HookServer.autoApproveTools` whitelist — plan-mode exit now prompts a real confirm dialog, and Settings → Behavior → "Auto-approve Tools" lets users toggle individual tools. See [`pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md`](../../pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md). Our merger continues to *additively* preserve every CodeIsland hook entry — no subtractive logic was added, because the upstream fix is the right path and the `PermissionRequest` hook is now a legitimate input source for the notch popup, not a bypass mechanism.
222	
223	#### Pattern A — Sidecar files (always-ignored)
224	
225	CLIs whose hooks live in a dedicated sidecar (containing nothing but CodeIsland hooks) are simply unmanaged by chezmoi. Concretely:
226	
227	| File | CLI | Why unmanaged |
228	|------|-----|---------------|
229	| `~/.codex/hooks.json` | Codex | Pure CodeIsland sidecar (also extended by Superset's notify.sh in some setups, but that's installed by Superset, not us) |
230	| `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | Cursor | Same |
231	| `~/.copilot/hooks/codeisland.json` | GitHub Copilot CLI | Pure CodeIsland sidecar |
232	| `~/.gemini/settings.json` | Gemini CLI | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
233	| `~/.antigravity/settings.json` | AntiGravity (CLI, not the editor) | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
234	
235	These paths are added to [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) as **always-ignore** so accidentally running `chezmoi add ~/.codex/hooks.json` won't pull a CodeIsland-owned file into the source tree (which would clobber the app's runtime updates and create a ping-pong with its auto-installer).
236	
237	If you later want to manage non-hook prefs in `~/.gemini/settings.json` or `~/.antigravity/settings.json`, write a `modify_` overlay that follows the hook-aware pattern below — and remove the corresponding ignore line.
238	
239	#### Pattern B — Mixed files (hook-aware merger)
240	
241	Files where stable user prefs and CodeIsland hooks coexist need a smarter overlay. Currently the only such file is **`~/.claude/settings.json`** — Claude Code stores model selection, plugins, statusLine, and `permissions.defaultMode` in the same file as `hooks.<event>` arrays. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays wholesale: declaring a `hooks.Notification` entry in our overlay would silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply`, then CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong producing diff noise and broken integrations.
242	
243	[`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) solves this with a hook-aware merger:
244	
245	1. **Non-hook keys** (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `statusLine`, …) deep-merge normally via `base * overlay_no_hooks`. Note: `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` is set deliberately to work around Claude Code resetting the active permission mode after every interactive prompt (`AskUserQuestion`, CodeIsland popup, remote-control inject); see [`pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md`](../../pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md). The deep-merge writes the `defaultMode` scalar without touching sibling `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays — those remain machine-local.
246	2. **`hooks.<event>` arrays** are merged additively: for each event the overlay declares, append entries whose `.hooks[0].command` isn't already represented in the live array (string-equality match). Live entries are preserved verbatim, no entry is ever removed.
247	
248	The full filter (jq):
249	
250	```jq
251	. as $base
252	| ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
253	| ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
254	| ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
255	| $merged
256	| .hooks = (
257	    ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
258	    | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
259	        $live_hooks;
260	        .[$ev.key] = (
261	          (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
262	          | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
263	          | $live_arr + (
264	              $ev.value
265	              | map(select(
266	                  (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
267	                  | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
268	                ))
269	            )
270	        )
271	      )
272	  )
273	```
274	
275	Test coverage in `tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`:
276	
277	- `claude modify_settings: notify.sh added to empty hooks, codeisland entries preserved` — proves the additive append works without removing CodeIsland entries.
278	- `claude modify_settings: idempotent when notify.sh already present` — proves no duplicate appears on re-apply.
279	- `claude modify_settings: empty live file produces overlay-only output` — bootstrap on a fresh machine.
280	- `claude modify_settings: non-hook deep-merge preserves siblings` — proves user-added plugins/marketplaces survive.
281	
282	> **Sibling overlay**: `~/.claude/keybindings.json` is managed by a separate, simpler `modify_` script — [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json). It is NOT hook-aware (CodeIsland doesn't write to keybindings.json). See [Claude Code keybindings](claude-code-keybindings.md) for its design, the `chat:cycleMode`-only mode-jump limitation, and how to add personal binding overrides.
283	
284	### Future work (deferred)
285	
286	- **Apprise-to-webhook expansion of `~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh`**: the script already calls `apprise --tag desktop` for local OS notifications. Could be extended to also fire `apprise --tag webhook` for remote chat-app delivery (Slack, Discord, Telegram, …) using URLs configured in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml`. Open question: noise filtering — should webhook fire on every `Notification`/`Stop`, or only on permission-request and session-end? Likely needs an env-var gate (`CLAUDE_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK=1`) so each machine opts in. Track in a separate change.
287	- **Managed overlays for `~/.gemini/settings.json` and `~/.antigravity/settings.json`**: defer until concrete prefs need enforcing. When added, follow the hook-aware merger pattern from Claude (each of those files also has CodeIsland-injected `hooks` blocks today).
288
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# nvim 0.12 startup ENOENT from vim.fs.find via avante / lualine / lazy checker
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	
5	- `vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory`
6	- `[C]: in function 'assert'` followed by `vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'`
7	- Source frames: `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (avante)
8	- Source frames: `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (lualine)
9	- Often paired with: `lualine: Failed to refresh statusline: ... vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT`
10	- Triggered from: `lazy/manage/checker.lua` (background plugin update check) or
11	  `lualine.refresh` immediately after startup
12	- One-shot at startup; nvim continues to function but the popup is noisy
13	
14	**First seen**: 2026-04 (Neovim 0.12.1, macOS, Apple Silicon)
15	**Affects**: Neovim **0.12.x** + LazyVim + avante.nvim + lualine.nvim. Did not
16	occur on 0.11.x.
17	**Status**: workaround = `cd` to a real directory before launching nvim. No
18	upstream issue filed (regression in `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua`).
19	
20	## Symptom
21	
22	Verbatim from a real session:
23	
24	```
25	Error  20:05:51 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
26	stack traceback:
27		[C]: in function 'assert'
28		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
29		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106: in function <...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:102>
30		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:167: in function 'detect'
31		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:206: in function 'get_project_root'
32		...al/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/suggestion.lua:43: in function 'new'
33		...4/.local/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/init.lua:425: in function '_init'
34		...
35		...al/share/nvim/lazy/lazy.nvim/lua/lazy/manage/checker.lua:43: in function 'fast_check'
36	
37	Error  20:06:04 msg_show.lua_error vim.schedule callback: ...share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine/utils/utils.lua:211: lualine: Failed to refresh statusline:
38	...ee84/.local/share/nvim/lazy/lualine.nvim/lua/lualine.lua:433: Lua: vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory
39	stack traceback:
40		[C]: in function 'assert'
41		vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'
42		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55: in function <....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:52>
43		....local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:106: in function 'detect'
44		...
45	```
46	
47	Both stacks bottom out at the **same** `[C]: in function 'assert'` →
48	`vim/fs.lua: in function 'find'` frame.
49	
50	## Root cause
51	
52	In Neovim **0.12**, `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` added an unguarded `assert` on
53	the result of `vim.uv.cwd()` inside the upward-walking branch of
54	`vim.fs.find()`:
55	
56	```lua
57	-- runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua, around line 716
58	local cwd = assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())
59	```
60	
61	`uv.cwd()` returns `nil, "ENOENT", "ENOENT: no such file or directory"`
62	when the process's current working directory has been **deleted out from
63	under the running shell** — the classic cases:
64	
65	- `git switch` / `git checkout` to a branch where the current directory
66	  doesn't exist
67	- `rm -rf` the directory you're sitting in (often via `yazi`, `oil`,
68	  `lazygit`, or another tmux pane)
69	- `mv` the parent directory away
70	- The shell that launched nvim was started in a directory that has since
71	  been deleted
72	
73	When `uv.cwd()` returns nil, the `assert()` raises, which surfaces as the
74	generic `vim/fs.lua:0: ENOENT: no such file or directory` traceback —
75	**with no hint that the real culprit is a missing cwd**.
76	
77	Two innocent callers happen to trigger this at startup:
78	
79	1. **`avante.nvim`** (`utils/root.lua:106`) calls `vim.fs.find(..., { path =
80	   M.bufpath(buf) or vim.uv.cwd(), upward = true })` from
81	   `suggestion.lua:43` during `_init()`. If `bufpath` is nil for the
82	   current buffer (no name yet, scratch, dashboard), the fallback hits the
83	   stale cwd.
84	2. **`LazyVim`** (`util/root.lua:55`) does the same pattern, called from
85	   `util/lualine.lua` on every `lualine.refresh()` — so the error fires
86	   continuously, not just once.
87	
88	The `lazy.nvim` checker frame (`lazy/manage/checker.lua:43 → git.lua:192
89	get_tag_refs`) is unrelated; it just happens to call `vim.fs.find` from a
90	scheduled callback at the same moment.
91	
92	This is **not** a bug in avante, LazyVim, lualine, or lazy — they all worked
93	on 0.11. It's a Neovim 0.12 regression: the new assert in `vim.fs.find`
94	turns a previously-recoverable nil-cwd into a hard error.
95	
96	## Workaround
97	
98	**Immediate (per-session):** cd to a directory that exists and re-launch
99	nvim:
100	
101	```sh
102	cd ~ && nvim
103	# or, from inside the broken nvim:
104	:cd ~
105	:e
106	```
107	
108	To verify which side is wrong (your shell vs nvim itself):
109	
110	```sh
111	pwd                    # if this errors, your shell's cwd is gone
112	ls "$(pwd)"            # confirm the dir actually exists on disk
113	nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())' -c 'qa!'
114	# nil = stale cwd, the assert will fire
115	```
116	
117	**Defensive (per-machine, optional):** add a pre-startup guard to your
118	shell rc — if `pwd` fails, jump to `$HOME` before launching interactive
119	tools. Not added to this repo's `dot_config/zsh/` because the failure mode
120	is loud enough to notice and the underlying state (`rm -rf $PWD`) usually
121	indicates the user already knows.
122	
123	**Code-level workaround (not applied):** monkey-patch `vim.fs.find` to fall
124	back to `vim.fn.expand("~")` when `uv.cwd()` is nil, e.g. in
125	`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. Skipped because (a) upstream will
126	likely revert/guard the assert, (b) silently rewriting cwd hides genuine
127	state corruption, (c) the trigger is rare in practice.
128	
129	## Prevention
130	
131	- Don't `rm -rf` or `git switch`-away from the directory a long-lived
132	  shell is sitting in. If you must, `cd ~` first.
133	- Tools that delete-then-recreate the cwd (some `git worktree` workflows,
134	  container rebuilds, `mise` cache resets) are the most common root cause —
135	  prefer `cd` out before the destructive action.
136	- If you see the symptom *without* having deleted the cwd, the next
137	  suspect is your shell's `chpwd`/`precmd` racing with a background
138	  process; check `~/.config/zsh/` hooks.
139	
140	Not graduated to a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant: trigger is user-action-driven,
141	not a config-level trap that recurs across machines.
142	
143	## Related
144	
145	- Upstream source: `runtime/lua/vim/fs.lua` line ~716 in Neovim 0.12.x
146	  (`assert((iswin and prefix:match('^%w:$')) and uv.fs_realpath(prefix) or uv.cwd())`)
147	- Affected callers in this repo's plugin set:
148	  - `lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/utils/root.lua:106` (`detectors.pattern`)
149	  - `lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:55` (also `detectors.pattern`)
150	- No upstream issue filed at neovim/neovim, avante.nvim, or LazyVim as of
151	  2026-04. If this recurs across multiple users, file at
152	  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues with the verbatim traceback and
153	  the `nvim --headless -c 'lua print(vim.uv.cwd())'` repro.
154
```

4	- In Neovim, every `:TSInstall <lang>` (or auto-install on open) prints the
5	  same error for bash, python, javascript, html, markdown, yaml, json5, regex,
6	  luap, printf, dockerfile, xml, rst, vim, diff, c, typescript, query,

12	        ^

15	      at onErrorNT (node:internal/child_process:484:16)
16	      at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:89:21)
17	  Emitted 'error' event on ChildProcess instance at:
18	      at ChildProcess._handle.onexit (node:internal/child_process:292:12)
19	      ...
20	      errno: -13,
21	      code: 'EACCES',
22	      syscall: 'spawn /home/…/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter',
23	      spawnargs: [ 'build', '-o', 'parser.so' ]
24	  ```
25	- `tree-sitter --version` from the shell reports a version normally (e.g.
26	  `tree-sitter 0.26.8`) with exit code **0** → looks healthy
27	- `ls -la ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/<VER>/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/tree-sitter`
28	  shows a **0-byte file** with mode **`-rw-------`** (0600) — not executable,
29	  no content
30	- `chezmoi apply` re-runs never reinstall tree-sitter: ansible's
31	  `treesitter_check` sees `rc=0` from `--version` and skips the install block
32	- Affected actions: `:TSInstall!`, `:TSUpdate`, any LazyVim auto-install on
33	  buffer open → red error banners, no syntax highlighting for the target
34	  language
35	
36	**First seen**: 2026-04 on `jingle-207` (Ubuntu 22.04, noRoot=true,
37	useChineseMirror=true, tree-sitter-cli 0.26.8 installed via
38	`mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli`). Traceable to an earlier apply
39	where the npm postinstall partially downloaded the prebuilt binary before
40	failing.
41	**Affects**: any host where `npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` postinstall
42	attempted to download `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/vX.Y/tree-sitter-linux-<arch>.gz`
43	and the stream was interrupted (GFW flakiness, CDN 503, connection reset
44	mid-gunzip). The postinstall exits 0 even on failure.
45	**Status**: detection workaround in
46	`dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml` (aggregate check =
47	`--version` AND native-binary `[-s && -x]`); recovery = `rm` the empty
48	binary and reinstall. No upstream fix; this is a silent bug in
49	tree-sitter-cli's `install.js`.
50	
51	## Symptom
52	
53	Open any file type in Neovim on an affected host:
54	
55	```
56	$ nvim foo.py
57	# red error banner appears repeatedly with the Node.js EACCES stack above,
58	# once per parser in the ensure_installed list
59	```
60	
61	The shell-level sanity checks all pass:
62	
63	```bash
64	$ which tree-sitter
65	/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/bin/tree-sitter
66	
67	$ tree-sitter --version
68	tree-sitter 0.26.8
69	
70	$ echo "exit=$?"
71	exit=0
72	```
73	
74	But the actual native binary is empty:
75	
76	```bash
77	$ ls -la ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/
78	-rwx------   303 Apr 22 23:16 cli.js        ← node wrapper (executable)
79	-rw-------  14k  Apr 22 23:16 dsl.d.ts
80	-rw------- 3.7k  Apr 22 23:16 install.js
81	-rw-------  749  Apr 22 23:16 package.json
82	-rw-------    0  Apr 22 23:16 tree-sitter   ← NATIVE BINARY, 0 BYTES, NOT EXECUTABLE
83	```
84	
85	Resolution path (mise shim → mise dispatcher → cli.js → native `./tree-sitter`):
86	
87	```bash
88	$ readlink -f $(which tree-sitter)
89	/home/ldw/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/cli.js
90	```
91	
92	`cli.js` is 303 bytes and IS executable — it's the thing that runs for
93	`tree-sitter --version`. When cli.js needs to do actual work (parser build),
94	it `spawn`s `./tree-sitter` relative to its own directory. That file is the
95	0-byte one.
96	
97	## Root cause
98	
99	Two bugs compound:
100	
101	**Bug 1 (upstream, tree-sitter-cli)**: the npm `postinstall` script
102	`node install.js` downloads a prebuilt Linux binary from:
103	
104	```
105	https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/v0.26.8/tree-sitter-linux-x64.gz
106	```
107	
108	This 302-redirects to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` (Azure blob
109	storage). On networks where Azure CDN is flaky (GFW, Cloudflare
110	interference, corporate proxy), the gunzip stream can:
111	
112	- Complete the TCP connection and create the destination file
113	- Read 0 bytes (or a partial, corrupt stream)
114	- Fail the gunzip pipeline silently
115	- Still exit `install.js` with rc=0 via Node's default unhandled-rejection
116	  handler
117	
118	Result: `./tree-sitter` exists, is 0 bytes, and retains the default
119	`fs.createWriteStream` mode of `0600` (which is `rw-` for owner, no exec
120	bit). The `fs.chmodSync(dest, '755')` call later in the script is either
121	never reached (exception swallowed) or was never there for the code path
122	that created the file.
123	
124	The related "this hangs forever" failure mode is already documented in
125	[`pitfalls/npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md`](npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md).
126	This pitfall is the **opposite** failure: postinstall doesn't hang — it
127	returns "success" with a broken binary.
128	
129	**Bug 2 (this repo, pre-fix)**: ansible's `treesitter_check` ran
130	`tree-sitter --version` as the liveness probe:
131	
132	```yaml
133	- name: Check if tree-sitter is installed
134	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
135	    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
136	  register: treesitter_check
137	  failed_when: false
138	```
139	
140	But `--version` in `cli.js` just reads `package.json`:
141	
142	```js
143	// cli.js (excerpt)
144	if (args[0] === '--version') {
145	  console.log(`tree-sitter ${require('./package.json').version}`);
146	  process.exit(0);
147	}
148	```
149	
150	It never spawns the native binary. So `rc=0` from the check is consistent
151	with a completely broken install. The downstream install tasks (gated on
152	`treesitter_check.rc != 0`) were therefore never triggered, and re-running
153	`chezmoi apply` on an affected host indefinitely failed to self-heal.
154	
155	## Workaround
156	
157	**Immediate recovery on an affected host**:
158	
159	Do NOT use `command -v tree-sitter` / `readlink -f` to locate the broken
160	binary — if cargo's version is also installed, PATH order may resolve to
161	cargo's healthy 12 MB ELF and you will delete the wrong thing. Scan the
162	mise install tree directly:
163	
164	```bash
165	# 1. Find + delete every empty / non-executable native binary under mise's
166	#    node installs. Safe to run even if no mise npm install exists.
167	for d in "${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs/node/"*/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli; do
168	  [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
169	  native="$d/tree-sitter"
170	  [[ -e "$native" ]] || continue
171	  if [[ ! -s "$native" || ! -x "$native" ]]; then
172	    echo "removing broken: $native"
173	    rm -f "$native"
174	  fi
175	done
176	
177	# 2. Reinstall via mise/npm:
178	timeout 180 mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
179	# If this SIGTERMs on "Downloading https://github.com/.../releases/..." —
180	# the GFW/CDN hang — skip to step 3.
181	
182	# 3. Fallback if step 2 fails (cargo builds from source via TUNA mirror):
183	cargo install tree-sitter-cli --force
184	
185	# 4. If npm left the mise package dir behind without its native binary
186	#    (cli.js present, tree-sitter native missing), copy cargo's build in:
187	mise_dir=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(ls ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/*/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/cli.js 2>/dev/null | head -1)")")
188	if [[ -n "$mise_dir" && ! -s "$mise_dir/tree-sitter" ]]; then
189	  cp "$HOME/.cargo/bin/tree-sitter" "$mise_dir/tree-sitter"
190	  chmod 755 "$mise_dir/tree-sitter"
191	fi
192	
193	# 5. Verify: both the mise path AND cargo path (if present) should work.
194	tree-sitter --version                                     # uses first on PATH
195	"$HOME/.cargo/bin/tree-sitter" --version 2>/dev/null      # cargo path
196	```
197	
198	Then in Neovim: `:TSInstall! <language>` should complete without EACCES.
199	(LazyVim's `ensure_installed` list will catch up on the next open.)
200	
201	**Structural fix (in this repo, applied 2026-04)**:
202	
203	Replace the `--version`-only check with a `--version` probe PLUS a direct
204	scan of every mise-installed tree-sitter-cli package, auto-purging any
205	whose native binary is empty or non-executable. See
206	`dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml`:
207	
208	```yaml
209	- name: Check if tree-sitter --version works (any install path)
210	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
211	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
212	    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
213	  register: treesitter_version_check
214	  changed_when: false
215	  failed_when: false
216	
217	- name: Purge broken tree-sitter-cli native binary in mise node installs (if any)
218	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
219	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
220	    set +e
221	    for d in "${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs/node/"*/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli; do
222	      [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
223	      native="$d/tree-sitter"
224	      [[ -e "$native" ]] || continue
225	      if [[ ! -s "$native" || ! -x "$native" ]]; then
226	        echo "BROKEN: $native"
227	        rm -f "$native"
228	      fi
229	    done
230	    exit 0
231	  register: treesitter_mise_cleanup
232	  changed_when: "'BROKEN' in (treesitter_mise_cleanup.stdout | default(''))"
233	
234	- name: Compute treesitter_check aggregate
235	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
236	    treesitter_check:
237	      rc: >-
238	        {{ 0 if (treesitter_version_check.rc | default(1) == 0
239	                 and not treesitter_mise_cleanup.changed)
240	           else 1 }}
241	```
242	
243	Why scan the mise install tree directly (instead of `command -v tree-sitter`
244	+ `readlink -f`): on a host where cargo **also** installed tree-sitter
245	(fallback path fired on a previous apply), `command -v` — especially with
246	`${HOME}/.cargo/bin` prepended — resolves to the cargo monolithic binary,
247	not the mise shim, and the "is native binary healthy" check would pass
248	despite a broken mise install. nvim-treesitter may still pick the mise
249	path at runtime (PATH order, plugin config), so cargo's working binary
250	doesn't rescue it. Scanning `~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/*/lib/.../tree-sitter-cli/`
251	directly handles BOTH the single-install host (fresh mise-npm failure)
252	AND the dual-install host (stale broken mise alongside healthy cargo).
253	
254	Downstream install tasks already gate on `treesitter_check.rc != 0` —
255	the aggregate fact makes the existing gates fire on broken-empty-binary
256	hosts without touching any other task.
257	
258	## Prevention
259	
260	When writing ansible liveness probes for tools that have **a lightweight
261	dispatcher wrapping a native binary** (tree-sitter, mise itself, rustup,
262	pyenv, many `uv`-installed shims), `--version` / `--help` is often a **false
263	positive signal** — it only exercises the wrapper, not the payload.
264	
265	Checklist when writing a new "is this tool installed" probe:
266	
267	1. **Does `--version` spawn the actual binary?** Inspect the wrapper script
268	   (often JS or shell). If it just reads from a manifest, you need a
269	   stronger probe.
270	2. **Is there a dry-run command that exercises the native binary?** E.g.
271	   `tree-sitter dump-languages | head`, `cargo --list`,
272	   `rustup toolchain list`. Prefer these over `--version`.
273	3. **Stat the resolved binary.** `readlink -f` through the shim chain and
274	   check `[[ -s PATH && -x PATH ]]` — cheap and catches both the
275	   empty-file case and the no-exec case.
276	4. **Don't trust postinstall scripts that touch the network.** Especially
277	   those that download prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases (see
278	   [`brew-cask-slow-github-release-assets.md`](brew-cask-slow-github-release-assets.md)
279	   and [`npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md`](npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md)
280	   for the "slow" and "hangs forever" failure modes).
281	
282	## Related
283	
284	- [`pitfalls/npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md`](npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md)
285	  — sibling pitfall: same install path, hang instead of silent-empty-file
286	  failure. Both caused by the same upstream hardcoded URL to GitHub
287	  release-assets.
288	- [`pitfalls/brew-cask-slow-github-release-assets.md`](brew-cask-slow-github-release-assets.md)
289	  — same CDN path, different tool (Homebrew cask). Slow but usually
290	  eventually succeeds; doesn't produce empty files.
291	- [`docs/tools/mirrors.md`](../docs/tools/mirrors.md) → npm postinstall
292	  scripts that download from GitHub Releases
293	- [tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cli `install.js`](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/cli/npm/install.js)
294	  — upstream source; no error handling for partial stream / zero-byte
295	  output case
296
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces
9	# arrays wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would
10	# silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and
11	# CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
12	#
13	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
14	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
15	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
16	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
17	# notify.sh while CodeIsland (or any other tool) freely manages its own
18	# parallel entries in the same event arrays.
19	#
20	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
21	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
22	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
23	#
24	# See: docs/tools/agent-overlays.md → "CodeIsland integration".
25	set -eu
26	
27	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
28	{
29	  "hooks": {
30	    "Notification": [
31	      {
32	        "matcher": "",
33	        "hooks": [
34	          {
35	            "type": "command",
36	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
37	          }
38	        ]
39	      }
40	    ],
41	    "Stop": [
42	      {
43	        "hooks": [
44	          {
45	            "type": "command",
46	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
47	          }
48	        ]
49	      }
50	    ]
51	  },
52	  "enabledPlugins": {
53	    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true,
54	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
55	  },
56	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
57	    "claude-hud": {
58	      "source": {
59	        "source": "github",
60	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
61	      }
62	    }
63	  },
64	  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
65	  "permissions": {
66	    "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
67	  },
68	  "statusLine": {
69	    "type": "command",
70	    "command": "bash -c 'plugin_dir=$(ls -d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); runtime=$(command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null); [ -z \"$runtime\" ] && exit 0; rt=\"${runtime##*/}\"; if [ \"$rt\" = \"bun\" ]; then exec \"$runtime\" --env-file /dev/null \"${plugin_dir}src/index.ts\"; else exec \"$runtime\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\"; fi'"
71	  }
72	}
73	JSON
74	)
75	
76	base=$(cat)
77	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'
78	
79	# Hook-aware merge:
80	#   1. Compute non-hook portion of overlay (everything except .hooks).
81	#   2. Deep-merge that into base normally: base * overlay_no_hooks.
82	#   3. For each event in overlay.hooks, append entries whose .hooks[0].command
83	#      isn't already represented in the live event array (by exact-string
84	#      command match on .hooks[0].command). Live entries are preserved
85	#      verbatim, and new overlay entries are added at the end.
86	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '
87	  . as $base
88	  | ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
89	  | ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
90	  | ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
91	  | $merged
92	  | .hooks = (
93	      ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
94	      | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
95	          $live_hooks;
96	          .[$ev.key] = (
97	            (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
98	            | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
99	            | $live_arr + (
100	                $ev.value
101	                | map(select(
102	                    (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
103	                    | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
104	                  ))
105	              )
106	          )
107	        )
108	    )
109	'
110
```

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: deep-merge a managed overlay into ~/.codex/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: Codex CLI rewrites this file at runtime, adding per-project trust
5	# (`[projects."<absolute-path>"]`) and marketplace paths
6	# (`[marketplaces.<id>]`) that are machine-specific. Tracking the whole file
7	# would create constant diff and bake one machine's paths into another's apply.
8	# We enforce only stable preferences (model, personality, [features],
9	# [plugins.*]) and round-trip the live machine state untouched.
10	#
11	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints
12	# the new contents on stdout. The merge runs in a small Python program because:
13	#   - jq doesn't speak TOML.
14	#   - mikefarah/yq's TOML emitter collapses nested tables into inline
15	#     `{ ... }` syntax and fails to quote keys with special characters
16	#     (e.g. `github@openai-curated`), producing invalid TOML on round-trip.
17	#   - Python 3.11+ ships `tomllib` built-in for reads; the inline writer below
18	#     handles the small schema this file uses (scalars, nested string-key
19	#     tables, no arrays-of-tables) and quotes every table key for safety.
20	#
21	# Merge precedence (later wins):
22	#   1. Stripped live (everything except [projects] and [marketplaces.*]).
23	#   2. Managed overlay (this script's $overlay heredoc).
24	#   3. Machine-local state ([projects.*], [marketplaces.*]) re-attached
25	#      verbatim so per-project trust survives an overlay churn.
26	#
27	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml
28	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (Linuxbrew/cargo-installed in the base ansible
29	# role; standard on macOS), which fetches a managed Python ≥ 3.11 if the host
30	# system python is older — guaranteeing built-in `tomllib`. Falls back to
31	# system `python3`, then to a no-op pass-through, so a fresh-bootstrap host
32	# without uv yet doesn't fail this modify_ script.
33	set -eu
34	
35	overlay=$(cat <<'TOML'
36	{{ template "agents/codex.config.overlay.toml" . }}
37	TOML
38	)
39	
40	base=$(cat)
41	
42	# Pick the python invocation. uv guarantees ≥3.11 → tomllib always
43	# importable; system python3 may be older but the script's own ImportError
44	# handler passes the live file through untouched if so. `--no-project`
45	# stops uv from picking up the dotfiles repo's pyproject.toml. `--quiet`
46	# silences "Installed X" log noise on first run.
47	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
48	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --python '>=3.11' python -
49	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	  set -- python3 -
51	else
52	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; skipping merge" >&2
53	  printf '%s' "$base"
54	  exit 0
55	fi
56	
57	# Pass live file + overlay via env vars; emit merged TOML on stdout. If
58	# anything goes wrong (tomllib missing on Python <3.11, malformed live file),
59	# Python prints to stderr and exits non-zero -> chezmoi skips the file.
60	CODEX_LIVE="$base" CODEX_OVERLAY="$overlay" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63	
64	try:
65	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
66	except ModuleNotFoundError:
67	    try:
68	        import tomli as tomllib  # backport for Python 3.10 and below
69	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
70	        print(
71	            "modify_config.toml: tomllib unavailable (need Python 3.11+ or "
72	            "`pip install tomli`); skipping merge",
73	            file=sys.stderr,
74	        )
75	        sys.stdout.write(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
76	        sys.exit(0)
77	
78	
79	def parse(text: str) -> dict:
80	    text = text.strip()
81	    if not text:
82	        return {}
83	    return tomllib.loads(text)
84	
85	
86	def deep_merge(base: dict, overlay: dict) -> dict:
87	    """Recursive dict merge; overlay wins on conflict. Non-dict overlay
88	    values replace base wholesale (lists are not concatenated)."""
89	    out = dict(base)
90	    for k, v in overlay.items():
91	        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
92	            out[k] = deep_merge(out[k], v)
93	        else:
94	            out[k] = v
95	    return out
96	
97	
98	def fmt_scalar(v) -> str:
99	    if isinstance(v, bool):
100	        return "true" if v else "false"
101	    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
102	        return repr(v)
103	    if isinstance(v, str):
104	        # Use basic-string with escaping. tomllib accepts both basic and
105	        # literal; basic is universal.
106	        return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'
107	    if isinstance(v, list):
108	        return "[" + ", ".join(fmt_scalar(x) for x in v) + "]"
109	    raise TypeError(f"unsupported scalar type for TOML emit: {type(v).__name__}")
110	
111	
112	def emit_table(prefix: str, table: dict, out: list[str]) -> None:
113	    """Emit a TOML table. `prefix` is the dotted header path (already quoted
114	    where needed); empty for root. Scalars come first, then nested tables."""
115	    scalars = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if not isinstance(v, dict)}
116	    sub = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if isinstance(v, dict)}
117	
118	    if prefix and (scalars or not sub):
119	        out.append(f"[{prefix}]")
120	    for k, v in scalars.items():
121	        out.append(f"{quote_key(k)} = {fmt_scalar(v)}")
122	    if scalars and sub:
123	        out.append("")
124	
125	    for k, v in sub.items():
126	        sub_prefix = f"{prefix}.{quote_key(k)}" if prefix else quote_key(k)
127	        emit_table(sub_prefix, v, out)
128	        out.append("")
129	
130	
131	def quote_key(k: str) -> str:
132	    """Quote any key that isn't a bare TOML key (alnum / `_` / `-` only).
133	    We over-quote rather than risk emitting invalid TOML for keys like
134	    `github@openai-curated` or absolute-path project keys."""
135	    if k and all(c.isalnum() or c in "_-" for c in k):
136	        return k
137	    return '"' + k.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
138	
139	
140	live = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
141	overlay = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_OVERLAY", ""))
142	
143	# Pull machine-local subtrees out before merge; re-attach last so they win.
144	state = {}
145	for key in ("projects", "marketplaces"):
146	    if key in live:
147	        state[key] = live.pop(key)
148	
149	merged = deep_merge(live, overlay)
150	merged = deep_merge(merged, state)
151	
152	lines: list[str] = []
153	emit_table("", merged, lines)
154	text = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line is not None).rstrip() + "\n"
155	sys.stdout.write(text)
156	PYEOF
157
```
</details></tool-use>

## Docs Structure & House Style Report

### 1. **`docs/tools/` Directory Layout**

The directory contains ~40 markdown files covering development tools, terminals, editors, and infrastructure. Siblings for the LSP page include:
- **Editor & agents** section (line 135–144 in mkdocs.yml): OpenCode, specify-cli, SpecStory, Claude Code keybindings, codexbar, LLM
- **Shell & terminal**: ghostty, warp, starship, fzf
- Other: tmux, sesh, agent-overlays, containers, networking, etc.

**Alphabetical ordering**: The nav uses title-case display names with lowercase file paths. Within subsections, entries follow loose alphabetical order (e.g., "Agent overlays" < "Agent pane discovery" < "Agent skills").

### 2. **mkdocs.yml `nav:` Block**

The `Tools` section (lines 114–169) uses hierarchical grouping:
- **Editor & agents** (lines 135–144) — where LSP naturally belongs
- **Shell & terminal** (lines 122–130)
- **Sessions & worktrees** (lines 131–134)
- **Git & DevOps** (lines 146–156)
- **Productivity** (lines 157–163)
- **chezmoi conventions** (lines 165–169)

**Entry format**: `- Display Name: file/path.md` or just `- file/path.md` if the filename is self-explanatory.

Recommendation: Insert LSP under "Editor & agents" as:
```yaml
- Language servers (LSP): tools/lsp.md
```
(Alphabetically after "LLM" or before "OpenCode" depending on convention preference.)

### 3. **House Style for Tool Docs**

**From `ghostty.md` (comprehensive ~90-line example)**:
- **Opening**: One-sentence intro with link to official project.
- **Managed config**: Explicit filepath (`~/.config/ghostty/config`) + source path (`dot_config/ghostty/config`).
- **Key settings**: Bulleted explanations of what's managed and why (e.g., `macos-option-as-alt`).
- **Subsections**: Use `##` for logical topics (e.g., "xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote hosts").
- **Pitfalls/gotchas**: Prominent callout blocks (`> **Note**: ...`) for caveats.
- **Cross-links**: At end ("See also: [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config...").
- **Code blocks**: Triple backticks with language hint (`` ```ini ``, `` ```bash ``).
- **Length norm**: 1–3 KB per page; subsections are bite-sized.

**From `direnv.md` (compact ~50-line example)**:
- **One-liner concept**: "loads per-project environment variables".
- **File paths table**: Points to helper file, zsh init, prompt config.
- **Copy-paste config**: Provides a recommended `.envrc` snippet.
- **Behavior notes**: Explains equivalence (what it *doesn't* do vs `source activate`).
- **References**: External links to upstream docs.

**Conventions**:
- Headings: `# Title`, `## Section`, `### Subsection` (never start with `###`).
- Relative paths in cross-links use `../../dot_config/...` or `../sesh.md`.
- Code snippets are indented or in fenced blocks; shell output shown in plain text.
- "What's NOT managed and why" sections appear implicitly in callout boxes or a dedicated "What is intentionally NOT managed" table (see `agent-overlays.md` lines 121–134 for the pattern).

### 4. **Image Embedding**

No screenshot images found in the sample pages I reviewed. The `docs/assets/` directory exists but contains only **CSS and JavaScript** (`copy-to-llm/` plugin files), not media.

**Conclusion**: This repo does not embed images in tool docs. If needed, the convention would likely be `docs/assets/img/` (following MkDocs Material convention), but none currently exist.

### 5. **Pitfalls / Backlog Cross-References Touching LSP, NeoVim, or Language Tooling**

**Pitfalls** (relevant to LSP/NeoVim):
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md` — Neovim 0.12 startup crash from avante/lualine calling `vim.fs.find` with stale cwd. Excellent reference for "what can break" in the plugin ecosystem.
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/tree-sitter-cli-empty-native-binary.md` — npm postinstall downloads broken binaries; detection via aggregate health check. Directly relevant to LSP language parser tooling.

**Backlog**:
- None explicitly mentioning LSP or language servers found in the search.

**Recommendation**: Your LSP page should cross-link to these pitfalls in an "Upstream plugins & pitfalls" section, especially the tree-sitter one (tree-sitter is a core LSP/syntax-tree dependency).

# =============================================================================

--
      - taplo
      - television
      - pandoc
      - tailspin
      - lnav
      - grc

# --- taplo (TOML language server / formatter) ---
- name: Check if taplo is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: taplo --version
  register: taplo_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install taplo from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - taplo_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (taplo)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest taplo release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/tamasfe/taplo/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: taplo_release

    - name: Set taplo architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        taplo_arch: >-
          {{
            'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'aarch64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ''
          }}
--
    - name: Skip taplo on unsupported architecture
      when: taplo_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "taplo skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Download taplo binary (gzipped)
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/tamasfe/taplo/releases/download/{{ taplo_release.json.tag_name }}/taplo-linux-{{ taplo_arch }}.gz"
        dest: /tmp/taplo.gz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Decompress taplo binary
      ansible.builtin.shell: gunzip -f /tmp/taplo.gz
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: true

    - name: Install taplo to ~/.local/bin
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /tmp/taplo
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/taplo"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

    - name: Clean up taplo temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/taplo
        state: absent

  rescue:
    - name: Warn taplo installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "taplo installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"

228	# tree-sitter-cli
229	- name: Check if tree-sitter --version works (any install path)
230	  # Search standard PATH dirs INCLUDING ~/.cargo/bin (cargo install target)
231	  # so re-applies don't reinstall on hosts that fell through to the cargo
232	  # fallback path. ansible.builtin.command doesn't honour ~ expansion in
233	  # PATH; use shell with explicit ${HOME}.
234	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
235	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
236	    PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}" tree-sitter --version
237	  args:
238	    executable: /bin/bash
239	  register: treesitter_version_check
240	  changed_when: false
241	  failed_when: false
242	
243	- name: Purge broken tree-sitter-cli native binary in mise node installs (if any)
244	  # tree-sitter-cli's npm postinstall (install.js) downloads a prebuilt
245	  # binary from GitHub release-assets (Azure blob CDN). On flaky networks
246	  # the gunzip stream can fail silently, leaving a 0-byte file with mode
247	  # 0600 next to cli.js while postinstall exits 0. `tree-sitter --version`
248	  # still reports OK because cli.js reads package.json — it never spawns
249	  # the native binary. Every :TSInstall / parser build then explodes with
250	  # EACCES. Scan all mise node installs directly and purge empty/
251	  # non-executable native binaries so the install block below re-runs
252	  # npm install and heals them. Does NOT touch cargo's monolithic binary
253	  # (different install shape, can't exhibit this failure mode).
254	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
255	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
256	    set +e
257	    any_broken=0
258	    for d in "${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs/node/"*/lib/node_modules/tree-sitter-cli; do
259	      [[ -d "$d" ]] || continue
260	      native="$d/tree-sitter"
261	      [[ -e "$native" ]] || continue
262	      if [[ ! -s "$native" ]] || [[ ! -x "$native" ]]; then
263	        echo "BROKEN: $native"
264	        rm -f "$native"
265	        any_broken=1
266	      fi
267	    done
268	    exit 0
269	  args:
270	    executable: /bin/bash
271	  register: treesitter_mise_cleanup
272	  changed_when: "'BROKEN' in (treesitter_mise_cleanup.stdout | default(''))"
273	
274	- name: Compute treesitter_check aggregate
275	  # Re-install needed if --version failed (no tree-sitter anywhere) OR
276	  # we just purged a broken mise binary (force npm path to re-download
277	  # the prebuilt native binary so nvim-treesitter can spawn it).
278	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
279	    treesitter_check:
280	      rc: >-
281	        {{ 0 if (treesitter_version_check.rc | default(1) == 0
282	                 and not treesitter_mise_cleanup.changed)
283	           else 1 }}
284	
285	- name: Skip tree-sitter-cli on armv7l (no working node and cargo build too slow)
286	  when:
287	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
288	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
289	    - target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
290	  ansible.builtin.debug:
291	    msg: "tree-sitter-cli skipped on {{ target_architecture }}: no armv7l node prebuilt; cargo build needs libclang and takes 15+ min"
292	
293	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm (Debian/Ubuntu)
294	  # The npm tarball comes from npmmirror (when useChineseMirror=true), but the
295	  # postinstall script `node install.js` ALWAYS downloads a prebuilt binary
296	  # from `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/...`
297	  # which redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com (Azure blob CDN).
298	  # That CDN is frequently unreachable / extremely slow from China, and
299	  # tree-sitter's install.js has no env-var override for the download URL.
300	  # Without an outer timeout the whole `chezmoi apply` hangs indefinitely.
301	  #
302	  # `timeout 180` exits 124 on timeout → treesitter_npm.rc != 0 → cargo
303	  # fallback fires (cargo crates.io is mirrored via TUNA when
304	  # useChineseMirror=true, so cargo path is reliable behind GFW). 180s is
305	  # enough for a working network (full install ~30s) but bounded enough not
306	  # to burn the fleet-apply outer budget.
307	  when:
308	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
309	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
310	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
311	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
312	    timeout 180 {{ mise_bin }} exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
313	  args:
314	    executable: /bin/bash
315	  register: treesitter_npm
316	  changed_when: "'added' in treesitter_npm.stdout or 'added' in treesitter_npm.stderr"
317	  failed_when: false  # Don't fail the play; downstream cargo task handles it.
318	
319	# cargo build of tree-sitter-cli requires libclang (via bindgen). Install on
320	# Debian/Ubuntu when we might fall through to the cargo path.
321	- name: Install libclang-dev for tree-sitter-cli cargo build (Debian/Ubuntu)
322	  # rc != 0 covers both: regular npm failure AND `timeout` exit 124.
323	  # `is failed` alone wouldn't catch rc=124 because failed_when: false above.
324	  when:
325	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
326	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
327	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
328	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
329	  become: true
330	  tags: [sudo]
331	  ansible.builtin.apt:
332	    name: libclang-dev
333	    state: present
334	  ignore_errors: true
335	
336	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via cargo (fallback)
337	  # Triggered when npm install times out or fails. Cargo pulls from
338	  # crates.io which is TUNA-mirrored when useChineseMirror=true (via
339	  # ~/.cargo/config.toml sparse index), so this path works behind GFW.
340	  when:
341	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
342	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
343	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
344	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
345	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
346	    if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
347	      cargo install tree-sitter-cli
348	    else
349	      echo "Neither Node.js nor cargo available for tree-sitter-cli"
350	      echo "Install manually: cargo install tree-sitter-cli"
351	      exit 0
352	    fi
353	  args:
354	    executable: /bin/bash
355	  changed_when: true
356	  ignore_errors: true
357

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces
9	# arrays wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would
10	# silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and
11	# CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
12	#
13	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
14	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
15	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
16	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
17	# notify.sh while CodeIsland (or any other tool) freely manages its own
18	# parallel entries in the same event arrays.
19	#
20	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
21	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
22	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
23	#
24	# See: docs/tools/agent-overlays.md → "CodeIsland integration".
25	set -eu
26	
27	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
28	{
29	  "hooks": {
30	    "Notification": [
31	      {
32	        "matcher": "",
33	        "hooks": [
34	          {
35	            "type": "command",
36	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
37	          }
38	        ]
39	      }
40	    ],
41	    "Stop": [
42	      {
43	        "hooks": [
44	          {
45	            "type": "command",
46	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
47	          }
48	        ]
49	      }
50	    ]
51	  },
52	  "enabledPlugins": {
53	    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true,
54	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
55	  },
56	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
57	    "claude-hud": {
58	      "source": {
59	        "source": "github",
60	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
```
